text: - Batch of 2025 4 4 Placements 4 Infrastructure 4 Faculty 4 Crowd & Campus Life 4 Value for Money Four years heavenly life. Placements: During campus placement at my college 90% of students from my department got placed. The highest package offered is 80LPA and the average CTC is something around 12 to 13 LPA. Mass hiring companies for civil services are Godrej and ICICI Bank. 70% got internship. Top role offered was a Data Scientist Role. Infrastructure: Classroom is fully equipped with Wi-Fi and AC. The college has a central library where all kinds of books are available. The food and other facilities like gym culture room TV room everything is good. Time to time a special dinner is provided in the mess. All states' major festivals are celebrated in college. Faculty: Faculty members are quite outstanding and highly qualified in their subjects. They are helpful too like you can approach them regarding taking guidance related to internship or for referral for higher studies too. Semester examination difficulty level is moderate to slightly hard. Passing percentage totally depends on the professor mostly it is in the range of 35 to 40% percent. Other: I have chosen this course based on my JEE Advanced rank. I got a degree in civil engineering from IIT Bombay. Civil engineering is the fundamental discipline for infrastructure development of any country and this fascinates me to take this course. Many events and fest keep happening on campus, like Mood Indigo and Techfest. Reviewed on 12 Oct 2025 Read More S Shlok Nemani Integrated B.Tech. in Electrical Engineering + M.Tech. in Communication and Signal Processing - Batch of 2024 4.6 4 Placements 4 Infrastructure 5 Faculty 5 Crowd & Campus Life 5 Value for Money Great campus life, and you get to work with top professors in varied domains. Placements: Placements are really good in the EE branch, with opportunities from all the domains, including Core, Development, CSE, Consulting, and Finance, being thrown open to the students, so no dearth of opportunities. For sure 90% of students get placements and internships, and any student should least worry about those things. You get all the top recruiting MNCs here for the interviews. I feel EE is at a bit of a sweet spot compared to CSE in many regards. Infrastructure: While new residential buildings are coming up, the existing hostel infrastructure is a bit old, so there are some issues in that regard, and students should be mentally prepared for that. Academic infrastructure, including classrooms, labs, and a library, is at par with what students should expect from a good college. Faculty: It may feel like teaching is done in the same way as we go through the schools, since it's mostly the lectures and then you go through the exams (pen and paper), so it may feel like the same pattern but after 3rd year you get many opportunities to be more research oriented and curriculum becomes more project based. Course is enough for students to be industry-ready if they put in enough work. Other: EE as a department will be much better due to higher batch strength, as well as if people take integrated 5-year course, they do get an extra year to spend on the campus if they like.

Placements : IIT, Bombay is recognised all over India for its excellent placement record. According to official statistics for the placement season 2016-17 by the institute, jobs were offered to IITB students in engineering, IT, finance, consulting, analytics and education sectors. Around 84% of the B.Tech students (out of total B.Tech registered), and 82% dual degree students were placed. The average gross salary was 11.41 LPA, and the average CTC was 13 LPA. The highest offers ran into the range of 1-1.5 crores (unofficial figures). Almost all major companies, like Google, Microsoft, and prominent PSUs recruit from IITB. The placement season was coordinated by a dedicated placement cell, IIT Bombay. About 1000-1100 internship offers are made every year, from companies and universities in USA, UAE, Australia, Singapore, Europe, etc. Infrastructure : IIT Bombay infrastructure is a hit and miss. While the public buildings like lecture halls, auditoriums, open-air theatre, labs and indoor/outdoor sports grounds are world-class, the hostels especially the old ones, are in a bad state. Maintenance is done regularly, however, some old structures (as old as 1958) are almost beyond repair. Overall, the infrastructure can be classified as okay. Mess food is one of the weak points of the college. Almost no hostel mess offers delicious food, with the quality of food ranging from eatable to almost pathetic. This has initiated the construction of hostel canteens for each hostel. There is also a fine dining restaurant inside the campus that provides affordable good dishes. There is one hospital that is adequate for treatment of minor injuries and common diseases, however, for more specific or serious cases, it is recommended to visit a specialist outside the campus. Faculty : The faculty at IIT Bombay are prominent researchers in their fields, almost all of them being PhD holders from reputed universities in India and abroad. However, not all of them have a great style of teaching, so lectures can go from boring to pure fun depending on the type of professor. Research opportunities are quite enticing. The student to faculty ratio is also healthy. Most of the teachers teach using a combination of the blackboard and lecture PPT presentation, sometimes performing live experiments for more clarity. The first-year curriculum is mostly general and includes courses in physics, chemistry and math with one-two branch specific courses. The courses get almost completely branch specific in later years. With internships, students can get ample industry experience. Other : IIT Bombay conducts Asia's largest college cultural festival, Mood Indigo, Asia's largest college technical festival, Techfest, and Asia's largest entrepreneurship summit, Summit. Apart from this, there are numerous technical teams like AUV, IITB Racing, Innovation cell, Pratham (satellite), Rakshak (UAV), Team Shunya, etc., that participate and win competitions all around the world. There are 10-15 cultural clubs ranging from dance, dramatics, fine arts to writing, quizzing and modelling. Overall, the extracurricular activity scene is amazing in the campus.

To be precise December 1-18 is the first phase of placements. Most of the students get placed during this phase itself and phase 2 starts from January and companies come in scattered manner till April. Usually, there is 65-70% people placed every year. Don't be misguided by this number as many people even after registering for placements drop out of them for their other career plans like MBA, UPSC exam preparation, higher studies, start-ups, etc. Also, this percentage is a figures which takes into account all Bachelor, Master and Ph.D students. So, if you are in IIT Bombay and want to get placed, you will be placed with all probability. Highest salary is offered by Microsoft and Google and they offer $100,000/annum which when converted to INR is 70,00,000. Earlier it used to be Facebook which offered around INR 1.4 Crore. Minimum salary can be as as low as INR 3 Lakh, but almost all of them don't go for it, as it is too low for an IITian. Average salary varies from department to department in IIT Bombay highest average salary being INR 16 lakhs for chemistry and INR 15 lakhs for Computer science department. Then comes electrical with INR 12 lakhs .Detailed Placement stats can be viewed on http://placements.insightiitb.org/2015 . Almost all multinational companies visit IIT Bombay. AT Kearney, BCG, PwC, Strategy and Co., Bain and Co. are the top most consulting firms that come to IIT Bomaby and offer around INR 15 Lakh/annum and offer Associate consultant Job. FMCGs like Hindustan Unilever Ltd, P&G, ITC and Mendeloz foods are regular recruiters of interns but come occasionally to recruit undergraduates and offer around INR 18 Lakhs/annum and offer supply chain management profile. Almost all Wall street finance companies like Goldman Sachs, JP Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Deutsche Bank come for recruiting and offer around INR 14 Lakhs/annum and offer Analyst profile. PSUs like HPCL, ISRO also come for recruiting where ISRO offered INR 8 Lakh/annum and HPCL offered INR 12 Lakh/annum and offer Assistant Manager. Other than these around 250 companies come every year for recruiting. All above mentioned companies come for recruiting interns as well. Highest Stipend offered is 1.25 Lakh/month by P&G and people do unpaid internship for experience. Average Stipend is 10,000/month. Infrastructure : It will not be wrong to say that IIT Bombay has the best infrastructure in whole country. IIT Bombay is 550 acres lush green campus which rich flora and fauna, peaceful from the "Chaotic Mumbai". Only the academic area is equipped with Wi-Fi and you will get the fastest network speed that you might have never experienced(around 40Mbps).Almost all Classrooms are air-conditioned(exceptions being classrooms in respective department, which are very old), with even power plugs in case you required to use laptops in class(YES! Laptops are allowed in Class) and charge your mobile. Classrooms have different capacities ranging from 50-250, which are located in one building called Lecture Hall Complex, which is relatively new. Labs are not World-Class but good for Indian academic culture. Many equipment is old and experiments are not updated from time to time. Library has been renovated recently and is one of best in India. Fully air-conditioned, digital search of books, subscribed to monthly science journals are some features of library. Medical facilities is not that good and works fine for small injuries. Most of the time, students are referred to outside doctors for any serious medical issue. Sports and games culture in IITB is very rich and IITB has one of the best sports facilities. It has Football ground, Hockey ground, running tack, Olympic Size swimming pool, Gym, 2 synthetic basketball courts, 4 synthetic Volleyball court, 1 synthetic Kho-Kho pitch, 1 synthetic cricket Pitch, 2 Squash Courts, 5 wooden Badminton courts, 2 cement Basket ball Courts, 2 mud Volley ball courts and many Table tennis tables. If you are sports enthusiast, you will definitely find enough opportunities to prove yourself. Hostel rooms are very old and small. There is definitely a space constraint which is a problem and many people therefore prefer library to study. But newer hostels like H-15&16(for freshers only) are very spacious and much cleaner than old hostels and every student get a single room in their final yea . Food is mess is better in hostels where mess is rum by private caterers and worse in mess run by government caterers. As every hotel has a canteen, where people can order at cheaper rates, food is not at all a problem. Older hostels have been coming apart in terms of structure. Small mishaps have been happening here and there, so all hostels are going to be renovated in near future. Even Co-scholastic culture is very vibrant in IITB. Faculty : Faculty are very knowledgeable but not necessarily good teachers. If you utilize every opportunity that IITB offers, you can gain a lot of Knowledge. Professors are always there to help. Most of them prefer an appointment before meeting them(by mail or a call). but they do not mind if you show up at their office uninformed. They are definitely qualities and knowledgeable and always engage themselves in research in their specialized interests and open to students who want to help them in their research. Most of them use Powerpoint presentations as teaching method and transfer the presentations to us after each lecture. The faculty to student ratio is 1:10. Most of the industry exposure which you will get is only through your internship. Other than this, there are few to none industry trips organised in the entire curriculum. Course curriculum is very basic and rarely gets updated. But there is always flexibility in learning and any student can take any course from any department as additional learning and some courses are relatively new and bridges latest development in science. Undergraduate Project is not compulsory so many students get almost no flavor of real hand-on research other than small course projects which professors give. Academic pressure is normal,but sensitive people succumb to even such medium pressure due to job insecurity, parents' expectations, etc. Therefore, balancing ones academics is very important here and people who have not been able to do that have committed suicide (3-4 people in last 5 years). Other : Overall, IITB is definitely an engineering college that every student aspires to be in and worth fighting for. After getting into IITB, a person sees the world from a different perspective and has plethora of opportunities waiting for him. Be it academic, cultural, sports IITB satisfies every person.

Only the academic area is equipped with Wi-Fi and you will get the fastest network speed that you might have never experienced(around 40Mbps).Almost all Classrooms are air-conditioned(exceptions being classrooms in respective department, which are very old), with even power plugs in case you required to use laptops in class(YES! Laptops are allowed in Class) and charge your mobile. Classrooms have different capacities ranging from 50-250, which are located in one building called Lecture Hall Complex, which is relatively new. Labs are not World-Class but good for Indian academic culture. Many equipment is old and experiments are not updated from time to time. Library has been renovated recently and is one of best in India. Fully air-conditioned, digital search of books, subscribed to monthly science journals are some features of library. Medical facilities is not that good and works fine for small injuries. Most of the time, students are referred to outside doctors for any serious medical issue. Sports and games culture in IITB is very rich and IITB has one of the best sports facilities. It has Football ground, Hockey ground, running tack, Olympic Size swimming pool, Gym, 2 synthetic basketball courts, 4 synthetic Volleyball court, 1 synthetic Kho-Kho pitch, 1 synthetic cricket Pitch, 2 Squash Courts, 5 wooden Badminton courts, 2 cement Basket ball Courts, 2 mud Volley ball courts and many Table tennis tables. If you are sports enthusiast, you will definitely find enough opportunities to prove yourself. Hostel rooms are very old and small. There is definitely a space constraint which is a problem and many people therefore prefer library to study. But newer hostels like H-15&16(for freshers only) are very spacious and much cleaner than old hostels and every student get a single room in their final yea . Food is mess is better in hostels where mess is rum by private caterers and worse in mess run by government caterers. As every hotel has a canteen, where people can order at cheaper rates, food is not at all a problem. Older hostels have been coming apart in terms of structure. Small mishaps have been happening here and there, so all hostels are going to be renovated in near future. Even Co-scholastic culture is very vibrant in IITB. Faculty : Faculty are very knowledgeable but not necessarily good teachers. If you utilize every opportunity that IITB offers, you can gain a lot of Knowledge. Professors are always there to help. Most of them prefer an appointment before meeting them(by mail or a call). but they do not mind if you show up at their office uninformed. They are definitely qualities and knowledgeable and always engage themselves in research in their specialized interests and open to students who want to help them in their research. Most of them use Powerpoint presentations as teaching method and transfer the presentations to us after each lecture. The faculty to student ratio is 1:10. Most of the industry exposure which you will get is only through your internship. Other than this, there are few to none industry trips organised in the entire curriculum. Course curriculum is very basic and rarely gets updated. But there is always flexibility in learning and any student can take any course from any department as additional learning and some courses are relatively new and bridges latest development in science. Undergraduate Project is not compulsory so many students get almost no flavor of real hand-on research other than small course projects which professors give. Academic pressure is normal,but sensitive people succumb to even such medium pressure due to job insecurity, parents' expectations, etc. Therefore, balancing ones academics is very important here and people who have not been able to do that have committed suicide (3-4 people in last 5 years). Other : Overall, IITB is definitely an engineering college that every student aspires to be in and worth fighting for. After getting into IITB, a person sees the world from a different perspective and has plethora of opportunities waiting for him. Be it academic, cultural, sports IITB satisfies every person.
